brief:
Al Jazeera English reports that Israel's far-right movement has embedded a hardline agenda so deeply into state structures that reversing it may prove nearly impossible, even if Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu loses power. The entrenchment spans policy, institutions, and governance in ways that observers say transcend any single political figure's tenure.

The reported difficulty in undoing far-right influence reflects how thoroughly the movement has integrated its priorities into Israel's administrative and legislative frameworks, according to the outlet's analysis of the political landscape.
dek: Israel’s far-right is accused of embedding a hardline agenda so deeply that reversing it may prove almost impossible.
title: Far-right ideology entrenches itself in Israeli institutions beyond Netanyahu
